verdict.rationale: Groq publishes a first-party deprecations policy for models and endpoints. When a deprecation is announced, it commits to a shutdown date, lists recommended replacements, distinguishes production vs preview lifecycle stages, and offers migration support. A changelog with RSS/email subscription gives a channel for notices. However, the evidence never states a guaranteed minimum advance-notice window before removal, so the 'advance notice' part of the story is only implied. missing for 10: a documented minimum notice period (e.g. N days before shutdown), independent or hands-on corroboration that deprecations were actually announced in advance.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on a documented deprecation policy with advance notice before a hosted model is removed

citations.quote: When we announce that a model or endpoint is being deprecated, we will provide a shutdown date on which the model or endpoint will no longer be accessible
All API deprecations along with recommended replacements are listed below
A reverse-chronological API changelog with RSS and email subscription
